card.intuition: A permission request is what the harness shows the user before executing a tool call that isn't pre-approved. Approve and it runs; deny and the harness reports the denial back to the model as a tool result - the mechanism for keeping a human in the loop on risky or sensitive actions.
card.analogy: A junior dev at deploy time: the change can't ship without a senior sign-off. Deny with a note and the dev reworks the approach; approve and the change goes out.
card.time_complexity: Every tool call costs an extra model provider request, because the tool result must go back to the model before it can decide what to do next - and an unapproved call adds a synchronous human wait on top.
card.space_complexity: The approval or denial arrives as a tool result and stays in the context window, competing for the finite token budget like any other result.
when_to_use: When a tool call is risky or sensitive and not pre-approved - pause and ask
When you want to steer the agent mid-decision - attach a message to the denial
When the agent sits blocked too long - pre-approve the safe tools so requests only fire on actually-risky calls
gotchas: Every request is a synchronous wait on you - an agent that asks constantly can't be left to work AFK
A denial arrives as a tool result, so the model reacts to it and changes approach or asks what you'd prefer
Approve on autopilot and approvals stop meaning anything - rubber-stamping protects nothing

steps.label: Produce
steps.annotation: The model produces a tool call that is not pre-approved.

steps.label: Check
steps.annotation: The harness checks the call against the permission mode and any saved approvals.

steps.label: Pause
steps.annotation: Pre-approved calls run immediately; otherwise the harness pauses and shows the request.

steps.label: Decide
steps.annotation: The user approves once, approves for the session, or denies - optionally with a message.

steps.label: Act
steps.annotation: Approve and it runs; deny and the denial comes back as a tool result the model reacts to.

exercise.prompt: Simulate the harness gating a tool call. Calls for tools not on the approved list must be denied instead of executed.
hints: Denied calls never reach the function - the harness reports the denial back instead
Adding a tool to the approved set lets it run with no question asked
exercise.test_code:
tools = {'read': lambda path: path, 'rm': lambda path: 'removed'}
approved = {'read'}
assert execute(tools, {'tool': 'rm', 'args': {'path': 'x'}}, approved)['error'] == 'permission_denied'
assert execute(tools, {'tool': 'read', 'args': {'path': 'a'}}, approved)['result'] == 'a'
approved.add('rm')
assert execute(tools, {'tool': 'rm', 'args': {'path': 'x'}}, approved)['result'] == 'removed'
print('PASS')
